## AC-3.3: non-generic named items without an entity

```sql
select count(*) from items where entity_name_raw is not null
  and entity_id is null
  and normalise_entity(entity_name_raw) not in
      (select alias_normalised from entity_aliases where method = 'generic')
```

Result: **0** (PASS).

## AC-3.4: methods and ASX codes

```sql
select method, count(*) from entity_aliases group by 1;
select entity_id, asx_code from entities where entity_type = 'listed_company';
```

- curated 522, asx 264, generic 6 aliases (each must be > 0).
- 243 listed_company entities, each with an asx_code in the snapshot (260 entities carry a code in all; banks, airlines and the like keep their own type).
- Result: **PASS**.

## Top-20 review (T2.7, 2026-10-02)

Checked by hand: no two v2 rows are the same organisation. Each row's aliases were read in
`entity_aliases`; the v1 column's duplicates (QANTAS/Qantas, Virgin/Virgin Australia Airlines,
NAB/NATIONAL AUSTRALIA BANK, CBA/Commonwealth bank, ANZ twice, AUSTRALIAN Super) each collapse
into one v2 row. Close calls, kept apart on purpose:

- **St.George Bank** (Westpac-owned since 2008) and **ME Bank** (BOQ-owned since 2021) are
  separate brands that MPs disclose by name, so they stay separate entities (renames merge,
  brand acquisitions don't: DECISIONS, T2.4).
- **Foxtel** and **ASTRA** (the subscription-TV industry body that hosts the hospitality) are
  different organisations, as are Telstra and Foxtel.
- `family trust` is generic in v2 (no entity), so it's absent from the v2 column.

The review found that the LLM stage had minted small duplicates of curated entities, for
example "Qantas" (`qf`, 7 items), "Westpac" (`west pac`, 5) and "ANZ" (`anz 50`, 2). The
join-by-name rule (`docs/v2/entities.md`, Method step 5) merged them, 34 merges in all. It
moved Qantas Airways from 1,598 to 1,609 items, Westpac from 959 to 964 and ANZ from 844 to
846. One near-match is left on purpose: Tower Limited (asx) and Tower Australia (llm) are
different companies.
